curriculum.title: Code Your First Web Page: The Joke Machine
curriculum.description: A short sneak peek for beginners of any age. Learn how tags work, then write your first lines of code with p and h1 tags on a playful Joke Machine page. Subscribe to continue and add a button.

avatar.handoff_to_practice: Your turn! I cleared the example — go write it yourself.
avatar.incorrect_feedback: Not quite — take another look and try once more.

lessons.title: Build a Joke Machine
lessons.goal: Understand what a tag is and the pattern behind every tag, then write your first lines of code: a p tag, an h1 tag, and a button tag, building a Joke Machine page one piece at a time.

avatar.text: Ready to write your very first line of code? Today you're building something fun: a Joke Machine. By the end of this lesson, you'll have a real web page that sets up a joke and reveals the answer.

flow.title: What is a tag?
flow.body:
A tag is a small instruction for the browser.

The browser is the app that shows a web page. It reads tags to know what pieces to build.

A tag can tell the browser:

- Make a heading
- Make a paragraph
- Make a button

Tags aren't shown as regular words on the page. They're instructions the browser reads behind the scenes.

avatar.text: A tag is a small instruction for the browser. It tells the browser what to build on the page — a heading, a paragraph, a button. Tags work behind the scenes; they aren't shown as regular words.

flow.title: Every tag follows ONE pattern
flow.body:
Here's the pattern almost every tag uses:

**Opening tag → Content → Closing tag**

Written out, it looks like this:

`<tagname>` your content here `</tagname>`

avatar.text: Almost every tag works the same way: an opening tag, then your content, then a closing tag which is same as an opening tag but with a slash. Learn that one pattern, and you can write tons of tags.

question.question: A closing tag looks almost the same as an opening tag, just with a slash added .
question.explanation: True — the closing tag repeats the tag name, but adds a slash to show it's ending.

avatar.on_ask: Let's test your understanding. True or false?
avatar.on_correct: Yes! Same tag name, just with a slash added.
avatar.on_wrong: Look at the pattern again — the closing tag reuses the tag name and adds a slash.

retry.hint: Compare the opening tag and closing tag in the pattern — what's different?

avatar.text: You've got the pattern down. Now let's actually use it — time to write your very first line of code.

flow.title: Step 1: Write a p tag
flow.body:
The `p` tag makes a paragraph — a regular line or two of text on a page. Opening tag: `

` Content: your sentence Closing tag: `

` Example: `

Why did the robot go on a diet?

`

avatar.text: First up: the p tag. It creates a paragraph, a regular line of text. Opening p tag, your sentence, closing p tag. That's the whole pattern.

question.question: Which tag creates a regular paragraph of text?
question.explanation: Right — p is short for paragraph.

avatar.on_wrong: Remember, p is short for paragraph.

retry.hint: Think of the word 'paragraph' — which letter does it start with?

code_example.code: Why did the robot go on a diet?
code_example.description: Watch a p tag come together.
code_example.explanation: Opening p tag starts it — notice it's wrapped in angle brackets. The sentence - Why did the robot go on a diet? - in the middle is the content. Then closing p tag ends it — same angle brackets, but with a slash right before the p, letting the browser know this tag is closing.

question.question: Write your first line of code. Write a p tag with any sentence you like in between the p tag.
question.explanation: That's it — you just wrote your first line of code. Opening p tag starts it, your words are the content, closing p tag ends it.

code_example.code: Why did the robot go on a diet?
code_example.explanation: Match this pattern: opening p tag, your sentence, closing p tag.
code_example.starterCode: <!-- Write a p tag with any sentence you like below -->

avatar.before_demo: Here's the code again written for p tag.
avatar.handoff: Now write your own — any sentence you like, inside a p tag.

retry.hint: Start with an opening p tag, type your sentence, then a closing p tag.

avatar.text: Nice work! For the rest of this lesson, we'll use this exact line Why did the robot go on a diet? as the p tag so everything lines up as we build:  You can always use your own words when you build pages on your own.

flow.title: Step 2: Write an h1 tag
flow.body:
You already know the pattern, so this one is easy. The `h1` tag makes the biggest heading on the page — great for a title. Opening tag: `

` Content: your title Closing tag: `

` Example: `

Joke Machine 3000

`

avatar.text:
You already know the pattern, so this one is easy.

Same pattern, new tag. The h1 tag makes the biggest heading on the page — perfect for a title. Let's give your Joke Machine a name.

question.question: The h1 tag makes the biggest heading on a page.
question.explanation: True — h1 is used for the biggest, most important heading.

avatar.on_correct: Yes! h1 is the big one.
avatar.on_wrong: h1 does make the biggest heading — that's what makes it different from p.

retry.hint: Think of h1 as the title of the page.

code_example.description: Watch the h1 tag build a title.
code_example.explanation: Opening h1 tag starts it, the title Joke Machine 3000 is the content, closing h1 tag ends it.

question.question: Give your Joke Machine a name. Add an h1 tag on line 2 just above the p tag.
question.explanation: Great — your machine has a name now, and your page has two tags working together.

code_example.code:
Joke Machine 3000

Why did the robot go on a diet?
code_example.explanation: The code shown now includes the p tag
code_example.starterCode: Why did the robot go on a diet?

avatar.handoff: Your turn — name your Joke Machine with an h1 tag, right above your p line.

retry.hint: Start with an opening h1 tag, type a name, then a closing h1 tag.

avatar.text: You did it — your Joke Machine has a name and a joke line! Up next, you'll learn how to add a button tag so people can click to reveal the answer. That's the next step in class, and it's waiting for you when you subscribe.
